svg.aria-label: How to write з: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing з
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of з (cyrillic), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase з demonstration, 03:34–03:39, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source note on variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 03:34–03:39 lowercase з demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, curves right around a smaller upper lobe, descends through the middle into a larger lower lobe, curls left along the baseline, and finishes through a small rising exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a looped digit 3 with an open left side and exit join; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a compact printed form with two open-right lobes and no exit join. This learner path preserves the source's upper-lobe-to-lower-lobe order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: circle the upper lobe, pass through the middle junction, circle the lower lobe, and retrace to the lower-right tip without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's small rising exit, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant either lobe differently.
